opening.argument: The presentation promotes BitClub as a paid Bitcoin-mining opportunity while attaching unusually large wealth claims to participation: the speaker says, "The thing is most people here can become millionaires in three years." It ties that opportunity to purchasing mining capacity, stating that participants have "paid for the money for 2000 hash power." The model is also expressly framed around investment and recruitment, describing people who can "come in, invest, and recruit." Most significantly, personal benefit is made dependent on bringing in others: "You must get a lot of new people. Only then can you help yourself." Combined with the presentation of participation as time-limited, these claims establish a recruitment-dependent paid mining scheme rather than a straightforward business opportunity.

citations.quote: The thing is most people here can become millionaires in three years.
At this time they have paid for the money for 2000 hash power.
The club does not seek rich people, such like you and me, who can come in, invest, and recruit.
You must get a lot of new people. Only then can you help yourself.
